source: In-game system map screenshots of three systems, captured in one sitting. Angles were read off the images by eye, so they carry a few degrees of error each; the user flagged that several bodies sit slightly ahead of or behind the alignments described in prose. That error is real and it does not matter: twelve bodies constrain a single unknown, and the fit residual below simply reports it.
capturedInstantFittedNote: NOT observed — solved for, from the nine relative angles. Stated so it can be checked against the real capture time; the fit degrades to 7.0 deg RMS at +-1 h and 9.9 deg at +-2 h, so a capture time known to the minute either confirms this or refutes the whole reconstruction.

blindClockCheck.note: The fit was given no date. It searched 2,160 days and returned one instant, and that instant fell within 2.4 h of the real clock — the screenshots having been taken some time before the message arrived. Landing on the correct day out of 2,160 candidates is the confirmation; the 2.4 h is inside what eyeball-read angles support but sits at the edge, which is exactly why the real capture time is still worth having.

rulerRefinement.source: A second pass over the same maps with a ruler, given as four ahead/behind relations rather than numbers.
statements: ZV-759a is a bit BEHIND Agamemnon (ZV-759d)
Hortus Station is about the same amount BEHIND Helion Prime (VH-331d)
Beanironia (VH-331c) is just a tad BEHIND Shiptronia
KI-439b is just a tad AHEAD of KI-439c
KI-439a is just a tad AHEAD of KI-439d
rulerRefinement.chiralityCorroboration: All four usable statements agree with 'ahead = decreasing map angle', which is the reflected frame the joint fit had already forced. This is independent of angle precision — only the signs are used — so it corroborates the chirality without leaning on the pixel reads at all.
rulerRefinement.timing: LIVE — the ruler pass describes the game within 5 minutes of the message that carried it, so roughly 2026-08-16T17:40Z, not the earlier screenshots.
rulerRefinement.variance: All relations carry about the same uncertainty, roughly the on-screen radius of a body's circle: about 4-5 deg in the original captures and about 2 deg in the zoomed KI-439 capture.

withdrawnBracket.claim: 2026-08-16T15:50Z to 16:41Z, 51 minutes, from the model's alignment crossings for KI-439a/d and ZV-759a/Agamemnon.
withdrawnBracket.status: WITHDRAWN — wrong, and wrong in an instructive way.
withdrawnBracket.why: It treated model crossing times as exact clock edges. A crossing is only as sharp as the model's phase, and KI-439a's phase carries about 23 deg, which at 5.6 deg/h is +-4 h on the crossing. The near-alignment idea is sound for measurement and backwards for prediction: a pair sitting within the model's own error of alignment is exactly where the predicted sign is least trustworthy.

rulerRefinement.shiptronia: Resolved to VH-331e. Beanironia confirmed as VH-331c, which independently ratifies the VH-331 ordering that radius ratios had left as the weakest identification in the set.

phaseErrorBudget.finding: The model's phase today carries 5-20 deg of error, and it dominates every other term including reading angles by eye.
phaseErrorBudget.cause: The epoch is ~4,720 real days back — 350 revolutions for KI-439d, 2,135 for KI-439a — so any relative period error is multiplied by the revolution count before it reaches today's phase. One part in 10^5 on KI-439a's period is 7.7 deg now. Periods derive from Kepler on five-significant-figure semi-major axes plus FIO star masses of unstated precision; KI-439a's stored axis has a half-ulp worth 23 deg on its own.
phaseErrorBudget.reading: Monotone in revolution count, slowest pair matching best. That is the signature of accumulated period error, and not what a wrong epoch or a wrong frame would produce.
phaseErrorBudget.epochUnaffected: The fit scores 5.8 deg; its nearest rival across 2,160 days scores 36.0 deg. Ten or twenty degrees of drift cannot reach another minimum.
phaseErrorBudget.fix: Per-body phase corrections from one timestamped map per system, offset = observed - trueAnomaly(t) with the reflection applied. Absorbs the accumulated error whatever its source. Two captures days apart would further separate a constant offset from a residual period error.

frame.convention: angles below are measured counter-clockwise from screen +x with screen y flipped to point up, i.e. ordinary math convention on the image as displayed
frame.chirality: the map frame is a REFLECTION of the model's perifocal frame — equivalently the model advances every body in the sense opposite to the map. Consistent across all three systems, so it is a rendering convention and not a per-system quirk. Reflection preserves distance, so no separation, damage figure or shipping distance is affected; it matters only when comparing model output to map imagery.
frame.fitTreatment: each system's absolute rotation is a free parameter, so only the three relative angles per system carry information; nine relative angles against one unknown (the capture instant)

identification.KI-439: map labels ARE the natural ids, so no assignment ambiguity
identification.ZV-759: Vulcan = ZV-759b, Deimos = ZV-759c, Agamemnon = ZV-759d, confirmed by orbit-radius ratios 1 : 1.56 : 2.97 : 4.72 against the asset's 1 : 1.56 : 2.85 : 4.44
identification.VH-331: Hortus, per the CX address and the STNS panel's MS VH-331. Promitor = VH-331a, Dreamerr Prime = VH-331b, Beanironia = VH-331c, Helion Prime = VH-331d, ordered by radius, plus Shiptronia = VH-331e outside the captured crop. Beanironia and Shiptronia were later confirmed directly, which ratifies the ordering; it had been the weakest identification in the set because the b radius ratio reads 1.22 against the asset's 1.37.

fit.model: raukkPlanetPosition at the shipped epoch, unchanged
fit.uniqueness: one minimum under 25 deg across 2,160 real days scanned at 0.01 d, from before universe commissioning through today. The 5.7182-day KI-439b/d alias lattice is broken: three systems with incommensurate synodic periods share no other common solution over the universe's whole lifetime.

conclusions.commonEpochVerified: MEAN_ANOMALY_AT_EPOCH = 0 for every body holds, to the 5-20 deg the phase error budget allows and no tighter. This is the first real test of it — see the note in star-heat-damage.md on why the 74-flight log could not test it at all. A per-body offset smaller than the accumulated period error remains invisible, and a fitted phase correction would not distinguish the two.
conclusions.absoluteEpochPinned: orbital zero is 2013-09-13T21:45Z, 4,719.72 real days before the fitted capture instant, and no longer only modulo 5.7182 days
conclusions.mapNotAtZeroAtCommissioning: universe commissioning sits 2,719.72 real days after orbital zero, i.e. 148.92 game years of orbital pre-history. At that instant the four inner KI-439 bodies span 295 deg of true longitude, where a zero start would place all four at 0.
